_comment: Which entity in a captured scene is a THING — something worth having as one asset.
DATA rather than code, for the same reason parts.json is: the answer is a CONVENTION of the site
being captured, not a property of the glTF or PlayCanvas formats. `things()` proposes a candidate
for every direct child of a scene's Root whose subtree renders something, which is right for the
content scenes and wrong for the app's own — and a new capture can always arrive shaped a third
way. Correcting one should be an edit, not a release.
Measured over twenty captures: 19 need nothing here beyond `exclude`, and one (susan) bundles a
figure with the room she stands in. Expect roughly that ratio.
Bump `revision` when you change anything — an import records which revision decided, so a change
says which captures are worth redoing rather than silently disagreeing with what is already in
_exclude_comment: The app's OWN scene, which every capture from this origin ships identically: 2049393.json holds
1,016 entities whose Root children are machinery groupings — a controller model, a gesture
recogniser, a store of tool prototypes, a trash bin. They render meshes and they are not things
anybody would place. Eight names, site-wide, written once.
Matched on the entity name, in any scene. A capture that legitimately has a thing called `TRASH`

Matched on the entity name, in any scene. A capture that legitimately has a thing called `TRASH` would need its own `captures` entry to say so. `ToolModeTools` joins them from nancy's scene — the same machinery under a name the other captures do not use.
_captures_comment: Per-capture corrections, keyed by capture directory name then by scene file. The value REPLACES
the proposal for that scene: name every thing you want from it.
susan is the one measured case where the convention bundles. Her Root child `aula` is a classroom
with Alice standing in it — `ModelParent` is the figure (15 pieces) and `EnvironmentVR` is the room
(14), and both are separately useful. Nothing in the graph says to split there; only a person does.
A LIST names the things; a MAP also renames them. susan's figure entity is called `ModelParent`, which is the app's internal name and no use as an asset label.

Naming a scene here is also how you drop one entirely: give it an empty list. nancy looks like susan's sibling and is NOT — her scene is 1947006.json with 46 clean skin-tone variants as Root children, and needs nothing. Guessed wrong once; check before adding an entry.
